Churches, Cemeteries & John Paul II

Armenian Patriarchate, Kumkapı – John Paul II, 1979

The least-known stop on the papal trail: on 29 November 1979 John Paul II came here to visit the Armenian Patriarch of Istanbul.

Theme
Churches, Cemeteries & John Paul II
District
Fatih
Period
1979
Visiting
Limited access

The story

On 29 November 1979 the Polish pope came to Kumkapı, an old quarter by the Sea of Marmara, to visit the Armenian Patriarch of Istanbul.

It was the second day of John Paul II's only journey to Turkey – a day filled with meetings with Christians of different traditions. He called on the Ecumenical Patriarch Dimitrios I, came here to the Patriarch of the Armenian Apostolic Church, met the Armenian Catholic community and said Mass in the Cathedral of the Holy Spirit.

How to visit

The patriarchal church and the Patriarchate's offices face each other in the same street in Kumkapı, a walk of ten to fifteen minutes from Yenikapı station (Marmaray and metro). The Patriarchate is a working church office and the church opens mainly for services – check times on the spot, dress modestly and do not take photographs during the liturgy. The church front and the Patriarchate's gate can be seen from the street. We found no plaque marking the 1979 visit.
